text: VODAFONE TURKEY Data Architecture Guardrail Policy 1. Purpose This document defines the mandatory principles, rules, and boundaries related to the design, implementation, and use of data architecture within Vodafone Turkey. The Guardrail policy creates a framework that ensures data quality, security, and manageability while supporting corporate growth and innovation goals. All data engineers, analysts, and stakeholders using the data platform are obligated to comply with this policy. The objectives of this policy are: To ensure consistency, reliability, and scalability across data platforms. To preserve the integrity of corporate data assets. To enable reliable analytics, reporting, and operational data usage. To prevent uncontrolled architectural deviations. To clearly define which team approaches which platform with which request. 2. Scope This policy applies

to: All data platforms including ODS, PRIME (Mobile DWH), VFNETDW(FIXEDWH), PEP_CLDS(Incentro), MIS, Data Lakehouse (Ozone-Iceberg), and Cloudera (Kaizen-HDFS). Structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data. All data consumers including BI, advanced analytics, AI/ML, and operational systems. Data integration processes, ETL/ELT flows, and API layers. All internal teams, vendors, and business partners. 3. Architectural Governance and Enforcement Compliance with this policy is mandatory. For architectural deviations, formal exception approval is required. Non-compliant solutions may not be promoted to the production environment. 3.1 Governance Structure and Committees 3.2 Enforcement Mechanisms All architectural changes must pass through Data Architecture Committee approval. Guardrail violations must be detected and reported via automated monitoring tools. In case of critical violations, production deployment is halted. An annual audit and

policy update cycle must be implemented. 3.3 Request → Production Ownership Flow All data development requests go through the following standardized flow: 3.4 Situations Requiring Architectural Review The architectural review process is mandatory in the following situations. In scenarios deemed necessary, the matter is escalated for evaluation by the Data Architecture Committee or IT Architecture Committee (ITAB). Guardrail Rules 1. Changes requiring Architecture Review must go through the architectural approval process before being deployed to production. 2. Go-live is not permitted until the architectural review process is completed. 3. Review outputs must be recorded in an auditable manner. 4. Critical architectural deviations are escalated for Data Architecture Committee evaluation. 5. Decisions carrying vendor lock-in risk must be submitted for ITAB

evaluation. 4. Guiding Architectural Principles The following principles are non-negotiable and form the foundation of all architectural decisions. 4.1 Reference Data Platform Architecture Diagram 5. Data Product Definition and Architectural Guardrail Rules 5.1 Data Product Definition A data product is a reusable and manageable data asset produced to meet a specific business need, with a defined owner and established quality criteria. Each data product must contain at minimum the following information: Business and technical owner Source system information Data update frequency Data quality rules SLA / data freshness information Security classification Lineage and metadata information 5.2 Data Product Guardrail Rules Data products must be designed on a domain basis. Duplicate data products producing the same KPI or metric must not

be created. Data products cannot be published without metadata and catalog registration. Data quality and security controls are mandatory. Lineage and data dependencies must be traceable. Data products must comply with naming convention standards. Schema changes must be managed in a controlled manner. Deprecated data products must be flagged via the catalog. Data products must be traceable within the scope of audit and observability. Data products without a defined owner cannot be taken to production. 5.3 Acceptance Criteria For a data product to be deployed to the production environment: Business and technical owner must be defined Metadata and lineage registration must be completed Data quality controls must be active Security classification must be performed SLA and data freshness information must

be defined Monitoring and observability integration must be completed 5.4 Data Product Lifecycle Data products must be managed in accordance with the following lifecycle: Request and Business Need Data Product Design Architecture and Governance Approval Development and Testing Data Quality Controls Catalog and Metadata Publication Production Publication Monitoring and SLA Tracking Deprecation / Archiving Process 6. Corporate Data Platform Layers Vodafone Turkey data platforms consist of seven main layers. Each layer has specific responsibilities, guardrail rules, and inter-layer transition conditions. 6.1 Operational Data Store (ODS - Oracle Exadata) Purpose Near real-time replication of source systems; fast access to operational data needs. Guardrail Rules Contains no business logic beyond technical harmonization. KPIs cannot be produced; direct BI consumption for corporate reporting

is not permitted. Historical reconstruction is not permitted. 6.2 Mobile Data Warehouse (PRIME - Oracle Exadata) Purpose Business-aligned, curated analytical data; time-dimensioned and historical records. Guardrail Rules Official corporate reporting and KPIs are produced exclusively from here. Time-dimensioned and historical data is maintained; metric definitions are centrally managed. Schema changes require Committee approval; backward compatibility is mandatory. Changes are subject to data architecture approval. 6.3 Data Lakehouse Platform (Apache Ozone + Apache Iceberg - Cloudera CDP) Purpose Storage and processing of raw, semi-curated, curated, and exploratory data. Guardrail Rules. Raw data must be stored unchanged; direct external access to the raw zone is prohibited. Apache Iceberg metadata format is mandatory. Usage for analytical purposes can only be done from the

Gold layer. The processing purpose and output target for the Lakehouse must be defined in advance. Changes are subject to data architecture approval. 6.4 Distributed Data Processing Platform (Cloudera HDFS) Purpose Distributed computing platform for large-scale batch processing and machine learning workloads. Guardrail Rules Production workloads are subject to resource quota limits; unplanned resource consumption is automatically halted. Datasets used for model training must be registered in the catalog. ML models deployed to the production environment must go through the architectural review process. Premium Reporting Platform (Incentro PEP_CLDS - Oracle Exadata) Purpose The platform for calculation, reconciliation, and reporting of premium and incentive processes. Guardrail Rules Only data flows related to premium and incentive processes can be directed to this

layer; general analytics or reporting workloads are not accepted. Systems other than Incentro cannot directly consume this layer. Data model changes are subject to incentive process owners and data architecture approval. 6.6 Financial Reporting Platform (MIS - Oracle Exadata) Purpose • The platform where financial data from all source systems is reconciled. Guardrail Rules Only data flows within the scope of financial reporting can be directed to this layer. Financial data outputs must have an audit trail; unauthorized data flows are not permitted. Schema and model changes are subject to joint approval from the finance unit and data architecture. 6.7 Fixed Data Warehouse (VFNETDW - Oracle Exadata) Purpose To serve as the central repository for all data flows (subscriber, network,

operations, etc.) originating from VFNET (Fixed internet infrastructure). Guardrail Rules Only data flows originating from VFNET (fixed internet subsidiary) can be directed to this layer; mobile network or other Vodafone TR sourced data cannot be moved here. When VFNET data needs to be consumed on Vodafone TR main platforms (PRIME, ODS, etc.), integration must be provided through this layer. A valid data sharing agreement and security approval between the two companies is mandatory for data sharing. Schema and model changes are also subject to VFNET data architecture approval. 6.8 Target Architectural Positioning of Big Data Platforms The following table has been added to summarize the positions of the big data platform layers in the new data lakehouse architecture. 6.9 Inter-Layer

Data Lifecycle and Zoning 7.1 Lifecycle Stages 7.2 Zoning Structure (Data Lakehouse Target Architecture) Note: The Data Platform Team is not a single team. It consists of developers from capability teams outside the Data Tribe. The purpose is to transport raw data singularly and ensure centralized control. 7.3 Data Lakehouse Usage Matrix 7.4 Schema Evolution and Data Contract Rules Schema changes in corporate data platforms must be managed in a controlled manner. Schema changes must be designed not to affect downstream systems. Guardrail Rules: Schema changes must be versioned. Breaking schema changes (that would break the existing system) require Architecture sign-off. Backward compatible changes (that do not break the existing system) may be

subject to an automatic approval process. Column deletion can only be performed after the deprecation (controlled deletion procedure) process. Native schema evolution features must be used in Iceberg tables. Schema changes must be automatically updated in the metadata catalog system. Streaming data schema changes must be managed through the schema registry. Datasets without a contract definition cannot be published in the production environment. Data Contract contains at minimum the following fields: Field name / Type / Nullability: Defines the technical name of the field, data type, and whether it can accept null values; mandatory for technical accuracy and consistency of the schema. Semantic Definition: Explains the business meaning of the field, how it is produced, and what it represents; ensures

different teams interpret the data consistently. Primary Key: The field(s) that uniquely identify a record; mandatory for upsert, CDC, and data integrity. Update Frequency: Specifies how frequently the data is updated (e.g., real-time, hourly, daily); ensures SLA and consumer expectations are correctly established. SLA: Defines data freshness, accessibility, and latency expectations; the operational commitment between producer and consumer. 7.5 Streaming Data Guardrail Rules Streaming data platforms are an integral part of corporate data architecture and require standardized usage for event-driven data processing scenarios. Guardrail Rules: Streaming ingestion must only be done through approved Kafka topics. An owner must be assigned for each streaming topic. Topic retention period must be determined according to data classification. Streaming pipelines cannot be deployed to

production without schema registry integration. Streaming pipelines must include a latency SLA definition. Replay requirements must be planned according to the topic retention policy. Streaming data cannot be directly consumed by BI tools. 7.6 Layer-Based Data Retention Policy Data retention periods in corporate data platforms vary by data zone. Retention policies must be aligned with the data classification policy. PII data retention period must be KVKK compliant. Datasets whose retention period has expired must enter the automatic archiving process. Retention policies must be approved by the data owner. Layer-based retention: 7.7 Event Schema Management Rules Schema management in event-driven architectures must be done centrally. Guardrail Rules: All event schemas must be registered in the schema registry system. Use of versioned

schemas is mandatory. Backward compatibility must be applied as the default policy. Breaking changes can only be made with architectural approval. Event schema must be visible in the metadata catalog system. Topic-level schema ownership must be defined. Event payload format must be Avro or JSON Schema. Streaming consumer systems must support schema evolution. 8. BI and Non-BI Usage Policy Business Intelligence tools (Tableau, Power BI, etc.) are fed only from GOLD (Curated Zone) and PRIME VID, Opermart layers. 8.1 BI Use Cases KPI reports. Dashboards and scorecards. Management and executive reports. Production of analytical insights. 8.2 Non-BI Use Cases Billing and charging. Financial reconciliation. Fraud and audit analyses. Regulatory reports. Operational controls. 8.3 Guardrail Rules BI reports cannot be directly

connected to raw data. Critical corporate reports must be fed from PRIME DWH. Self-service BI usage is limited to approved data domains; report ownership and currency are monitored by the data steward. BI platforms cannot be used for non-BI purposes. (Exceptions must be subject to approval.) Non-BI use cases cannot be dependent on reporting layers. Data science and ML workloads use Cloudera and Lakehouse platforms. The use of streaming architecture is mandatory for real-time analytics. In cases of request ambiguity, it is classified as non-BI. 8.4 Semantic Layer Management Rules The semantic layer is the sole authoritative layer for corporate KPI production. Guardrail Rules: KPI definitions must be managed through the semantic layer. The same KPI cannot be redefined in

different semantic layers. KPI changes require Architecture sign-off. Semantic layer datasets must be registered in the catalog system. Semantic layer changes must comply with the backward compatibility principle. KPI production from outside the semantic layer cannot be used for corporate reporting. 9. Data Responsibilities and Approval Processes 9.1 Data Responsibilities Three mandatory roles are defined for each corporate dataset: Data Owner — business responsibility. Data Steward — definition and quality. Data Custodian — technical management. Guardrail Rules Datasets without defined ownership cannot be promoted to corporate layers. (VID, Gold Layer) Ownership information must be recorded and auditable. 9.2 Architectural Decision Authority Matrix The following matrix defines which role has approval, advisory, or implementation responsibility at critical decision points within corporate

data architecture. Guardrail Rules 1. Data Owner approval is mandatory for all changes affecting business meaning. 2. Data Architect approval is mandatory for all changes affecting corporate architecture. 3. New technology or vendor decisions are subject to ITAB evaluation. 4. Architectural guardrail exceptions must be recorded and auditable. 5. In situations outside the authority matrix, the Data Architecture Committee assumes the role of arbitrator. 10. Data Quality, Lineage, and Documentation 10.1 Data Quality Guardrails The minimum quality score for critical data assets is set at 99.9%. Datasets whose quality score drops below 90% are automatically quarantined. Quality rules are defined as code and kept in the version control system. Quality metrics are visible on real-time monitoring dashboards. 10.2 Lineage Requirements

End-to-end lineage from source to consumer must be provided. Table-level lineage is the minimum requirement; column-level lineage is mandatory for critical assets. Lineage information is stored in the central catalog system and made accessible. 10.3 Documentation Standards For each data asset: owner information, business definition, update frequency, quality rules. For each pipeline: source-target information, transformation logic, runtime, and dependencies. Business and technical metadata are mandatory. Documentation-first approach: Documentation must be completed before the data asset. 10.4 Data Observability Guardrail Rules Kurumsal veri platformlarında tüm pipeline’lar observability kapsamına alınmalıdır. Guardrail Rules: Pipeline failure monitoring is mandatory. Dataset freshness metrics must be monitored. Volume anomaly detection must be applied. Schema drift detection must be applied for critical datasets. (with schema registry) Data

completeness monitoring is mandatory for critical datasets. (record count, null ratio, mandatory field check) Observability dashboards must be accessible on a per-platform basis. An alert mechanism must be defined for critical datasets. 10.5 Data Freshness and SLA Rules Corporate datasets cannot be published in the production environment without an SLA definition. Guardrail Rules: Minimum SLA definitions by dataset type should be as follows. Additional rules: SLA violations must be automatically reported. Datasets without an SLA definition are not accepted as corporate data. SLA changes are subject to data owner approval. 11. Security, Privacy, and Compliance 11.1 Data Classification 11.2 Security Guardrails Data classification must be applied across all platforms. Authorization is performed according to the least privilege principle. Personal and

sensitive data must comply with legal regulations and Vodafone group policies. Masking and anonymization rules are mandatory. 11.3 PII and KVKK Guardrails Personal data cannot be used for analytical purposes in the raw zone without anonymization. Every asset containing PII data must be defined in the KVKK record. Data transfer abroad requires a legal framework and Committee approval. 11.4 Data Access Model Guardrail Rules Corporate data accesses must be managed according to the least privilege principle. Guardrail Rules: Role-based access control is mandatory. Column-level masking must be applied to PII datasets. Row-level filtering must be applied on a domain basis. Cross-domain data accesses are subject to approval. External data sharing requires a security review. Access logs must be stored centrally.

Privileged access must be reviewed annually. 12. Corporate Technologies and Tool Independence Per the Tool Independence principle, platform design must not be dependent on a specific vendor. Guardrail Rules Architectural decisions cannot be tool-driven; tools serve the architecture, not the other way around. Business logic must be portable and documented. Portability analysis is mandatory for solutions using vendor-specific formats or features. Open source and open standards (Apache Iceberg, Parquet, Avro, etc.) are preferred. Acceptance of a new vendor or tool requires Architecture Committee approval and evaluation. A transition plan must be prepared in advance for tools whose SLA, support, or license period has expired. Vendor lock-in must be actively prevented. 12.1 Approved Technology Stack Note: Data formats such as JSON,

CSV, etc. can only be used in ingestion and raw data layers. When data is moved to silver and gold layers, one of the above file formats must be selected. 12.2 Corporate Technology Domains 12.2.1 Platform & Infrastructure 12.2.2 Data Processing and Integration 12.2.3 Reporting and Masking 12.2.4 Governance, Security, and Quality 12.3 Storage and Compute Usage Storage and compute resources in corporate data platforms must be used in a controlled manner. Guardrail Rules: Compute quota must be defined on a per-platform basis. Unplanned resource consumption must be automatically limited. Idle datasets must be archived. Temporary datasets must be cleaned up within the scope of the retention policy. Storage tiering policies must be applied. High-volume datasets must be managed within

the scope of a lifecycle policy. Compute-intensive workloads must be run in the layer appropriate for the execution platform. 13. This matrix clarifies which data goes where. 14. Exception Management Situations requiring deviation from the guardrail rules specified in this policy are managed with

the following procedure. Exceptions are temporary; a formal request, business justification, and end date are mandatory. 15. Targeted Competency Development Areas The items in this section define the planned corporate competency development areas to achieve the targeted maturity level of the existing guardrail policy. The goal is to make data governance, architectural control, and operational traceability processes as standardized, centralized, and automated as possible. 15.1 Automated Guardrail Controls It is targeted to detect guardrail violations in corporate data platforms through automated mechanisms rather than manual controls. Critical violations such as schema incompatibility, missing lineage, SLA violation, missing catalog registration, or unauthorized access are expected to be automatically audited through control mechanisms integrated into CI/CD and deployment processes. 15.2 Centralized Schema

Registry Structure It is targeted that schema definitions used across all data platforms are managed through a centralized registry structure. Schema versioning, compatibility control, and contract validations in streaming, batch, and data sharing processes are expected to be managed with common standards. 15.3 Automated Lineage Collection It is targeted that end-to-end lineage information of corporate data movements is created automatically. Data flows from source systems to the reporting layer are expected to be transferred to the central catalog platform without manual intervention and data dependencies are expected to become traceable in real-time. 15.4 Centralized SLA Monitoring It is targeted that SLA and data freshness controls for corporate datasets are monitored through a centralized observability infrastructure. SLA violations, delays, data deficiencies,

and freshness problems are expected to be communicated to the relevant teams and data owners through automatic alarm mechanisms. 15.5 Cross-platform Retention Enforcement It is targeted that retention policies applied across different data platforms are managed with centralized standards. Hot/cold storage, archiving, deletion, and KVKK-compliant retention processes are expected to be applied with common control mechanisms across all platforms. 15.6 Governance Workflow Automation It is targeted that data governance processes operate independently of manual operations, in a workflow-based and auditable manner. Architecture sign-off, metadata approval, DQ control, schema approval, and governance review processes are expected to be executed through automated workflows integrated with Jira, catalog, and CI/CD systems.
